name: i2p
desc: Anonymous overlay network - a network within a network
why: A full anonymous overlay network running inside the internet, a fascinating door into garlic routing and peer-to-peer anonymity.

brief.what_it_is: I2P (Invisible Internet Project) is a decentralized, privacy-focused network for communicating and sharing information anonymously. It routes data through multiple encrypted layers across volunteer-operated nodes, hiding both the sender's and receiver's locations. The homepage pitches it as a self-contained ecosystem for private websites, messaging, and data sharing, with no central servers controlling routing. The brew package installs the executables eepget and i2prouter, though I did not confirm their usage from the pages I read.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage frames I2P as a secure, censorship-resistant network for anonymous communication and sharing, where blocking is hard because the architecture is decentralized. It describes itself as open source and maintained by volunteers worldwide.
brief.how_it_works: Traffic is wrapped in multiple encryption layers and relayed through a mesh of volunteer routers, so no single node sees both ends. The homepage says no central servers control routing. The docs index lists pages on Garlic Routing and Tunnel Routing, but I did not open them, so I cannot describe those mechanisms in detail.
brief.install_notes: The install docs page I fetched (geti2p.net/en/docs/install) returned only the documentation index, not installation steps, so I have no verified commands or first-run steps. The docs index lists per-platform guides (Debian and Ubuntu, macOS, Windows), a Web Browser Configuration guide, and a Router Console Configuration Guide, none of which I opened. Nothing about hardware or accounts was confirmed.
brief.standout: I2P is a complete network inside the internet rather than an anonymizing proxy to the open web: the docs list services that run over it, such as I2P Mail, IRC over I2P, and BitTorrent over I2P, plus its own address book and eepsites. The scout note's 'garlic routing' is the docs' name for its message-bundling scheme, which I did not verify beyond the index listing.
brief.status: maintained. The homepage lists I2P 2.13.0 as the latest update (dated 2026-07-20), preceded by 2.12.0 (2026-04-20) and 2.11.0 (2026-02-09), and claims 20+ years active and 40K+ active routers. I did not check a GitHub repo or commit history.
brief.caveats: I found no README or repository text, so the command list is empty rather than guessed. The install guide I fetched did not contain installation content, so setup details are unverified. I did not read the licensing page, so licensing is unknown. The homepage is marketing-style copy, so its claims (such as censorship resistance) are the project's own framing and I did not test them.

entry.title: I2P
entry.tldr: A full anonymous network running inside the internet, with its own sites, mail, IRC and torrents, routed through volunteer peers.
entry.deeper_look:
I2P, the Invisible Internet Project, is an overlay network: a network built on top of the ordinary internet that has its own addressing and routing. Traffic is wrapped in several layers of encryption and relayed through a mesh of volunteer-run routers, so no single node sees both the sender and the receiver. In the project's words, "Your IP and identity are hidden from the network itself."

The homepage says no central servers control routing. Every participant runs a router that also relays for others. That is the trade at the heart of the design: you get anonymity by becoming part of the crowd that provides it. The homepage cites 40K+ active routers and more than 20 years of activity.

I2P is mostly a place to host and reach services inside the network, not a proxy for browsing the open web. The docs list I2P Mail, IRC over I2P, BitTorrent over I2P, an address book, and eepsites (websites that live only on I2P). The docs index also has pages on Garlic Routing and Tunnel Routing, the mechanisms behind the message bundling and path building. That is where the real reading starts.

The brew package installs two executables: `i2prouter`, which appears to be the router launcher, and `eepget`, whose usage I could not confirm from the pages read. Both need Java, which brew pulls in as a dependency.
entry.install:
brew install i2p
# Pulls in openjdk and java-service-wrapper. Setup steps after install are not verified; the docs index lists per-platform guides and a Router Console Configuration Guide at geti2p.net/en/docs.

try_this.what_happens: Prints the usage for the router launcher, which shows how to start and stop the router.
Prints the usage for eepget, the other installed tool, so you can see what it fetches and how.

entry.whats_unique: It is a complete network with its own services, not an anonymizing gateway to the regular web. Every user's router also relays traffic for others.
entry.caveats: I could not verify setup steps or the command list from the pages read, and the anonymity claims are the project's own framing, so read the docs before trusting it with anything that matters.
